question: What is the main goal of maintaining environmental hygiene in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the cleaning staff
options.B: To make the hospital look attractive to visitors
options.C: To prevent the spread of infections and promote healing
options.D: To lower the financial cost of hospital maintenance

explanation: Environmental hygiene focuses heavily on eliminating pathogens to protect vulnerable patients and speed up their recovery. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is the hospital ward often described as an ecosystem during patient care?

options.A: It operates completely independently of the outside world
options.B: Air, water, surfaces, and human activities constantly interact within it
options.C: It has a controlled climate that never changes
options.D: It is primarily a living space for wild plants and animals

explanation: The ward environment involves a constant exchange between physical elements and people, which directly impacts health outcomes. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which physical factor in the ward helps to regulate a patient's natural circadian rhythm?
explanation: Exposure to natural light helps the human body maintain its normal sleep-wake cycle during admission. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h2)

question: How does too much noise in a hospital ward affect a patient?

options.A: It disrupts sleep and can raise blood pressure
options.B: It increases germs on ward surfaces
options.D: It speeds up the breakdown of intravenous drugs

explanation: High noise levels cause physical stress, interfering with the rest required for tissue repair and healing. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h2)

question: Where should used injection needles and blades be thrown away immediately after use?

options.A: In a paper envelope on the medication tray
options.B: In an open plastic bucket on the trolley
options.C: In a black general waste bin

explanation: Sharps must always go into a rigid, puncture-resistant container to prevent accidental injuries to staff and handlers. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h3)

question: A nurse finishes dressing a wound soaked with blood and pus. Where should this soiled dressing go?
explanation: Items contaminated with body fluids carry biological hazards and belong in the designated infectious waste receptacle. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is the main reason for having a reliable running water supply in a health facility?

options.A: To lower the cost of purchasing bottled water for staff
options.B: To keep the hospital floors continuously flooded
options.C: To enable effective hand hygiene between patient contacts
options.D: To reduce the overall electricity consumption of the ward

explanation: Water is essential for handwashing, which remains the single most effective way to stop cross-infection in wards. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is poor food handling especially dangerous for new mothers in the maternity ward?

options.A: It invalidates their daily nursing care plan
options.B: It leads to immediate staining of hospital bed linens
options.C: It can cause severe food poisoning that threatens fragile health
options.D: It increases the humidity levels inside the maternity unit

explanation: Postpartum women and newborns have delicate immune systems that struggle to fight off foodborne infections. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which task best describes a nurse acting as an environmental manager in the ward?

options.A: Supervising cleaning routines and monitoring ward conditions
options.B: Managing the water treatment plant outside the hospital
options.C: Designing the architectural blueprint for new hospital buildings
options.D: Personally manufacturing all chemical disinfectants used in the unit

explanation: Nurses oversee daily cleanliness, coordinate cleaning staff, and spot environmental hazards before they harm patients. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is an effective way for a nurse to involve patient relatives in keeping the ward clean?

options.A: Educating them on proper handwashing and waste disposal
options.B: Prohibiting them from visiting the clinical area entirely
options.C: Asking them to scrub the ward floors every morning
options.D: Requiring them to bring their own cleaning chemicals from home

explanation: Teaching visitors basic hygiene practices helps maintain a clean environment and prevents the introduction of outside contaminants. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h5)
